blocks.html: Fifthly, the accused having been, for other deeds, made prisoner by authority of the Seneschal of Toulouse, and at the instance of Jean d'Escornebœuf, called the Cadet — the said Pierre Guerre always underhand supplying every favour and aid — this deed too was advanced against him; whereof the same de Rols complained incessantly against the said Pierre Guerre and his wife, who wished to constrain her to accuse the same accused, being resolved to have him put to death, or at the least to have him put in the Galleys. And when he had come out of prison, by virtue of the interlocutory order upon contrary facts [appointement de contraires: an order admitting the parties to prove their contrary allegations] given by the said Seneschal, being back at Artigat, the said de Rols received him and made much of him as her husband; and as soon as he had arrived, gave him a white shirt, nay, washed his feet, and afterwards they lay together.
